# Momo Whisper

> Momo Whisper (formerly Whisper Momo) is a free macOS menu-bar app for voice dictation and translation, currently in **public beta**. Hold Fn to dictate into any app, hold Fn+Shift to speak one language and have it typed in another (for example, speak Thai and type English), or highlight any text to translate it in place. It was made by a Thai designer for Thai speakers who work in English, and it supports 16 languages. It runs on Groq with your own free Groq API key (optional: without one it works in on-device Local mode; translation needs a key).

Key facts:

- **What it does:** press-and-hold voice typing for the Mac. Speak, release, and the cleaned-up text is typed right where your cursor is, in any app (browser, chat, email, docs).
- **Who it's for:** Thai speakers on a Mac who write in English at work, and anyone who wants dictation plus translation in one menu-bar app.
- **Three modes:**
  - Hold **Fn**: dictate in the language you speak.
  - Hold **Fn+Shift**: speak and get it typed translated into the target language you picked. The source language is auto-detected.
  - **Highlight to translate:** select text in any app, click the floating button, and the translation appears next to it. Pick any of the 16 target languages in the popup.
- **Languages (16):** Thai, English, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Malay, Hindi, Arabic, Russian.
- **Tone control:** six tones for Thai and English: Email, Professional, Workplace Chat, Casual, AI-prompt, No-filter. Other languages translate in a clean, natural style.
- **Personal dictionary:** teach it names and jargon the recognizer keeps missing (product names, teammates, Thai nicknames), and it fixes the mis-spellings from then on.
- **Screen context (optional):** Momo can read a little text near your cursor (names, terms, the chat you're replying to) so it spells them right. On-device, never stored; can be turned off.
- **Connect your AI (MCP, optional):** Momo ships a local MCP server (`/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp`, stdio; its only outbound call is `send_feedback`, after you approve). Claude Desktop installs it in one click (momo-whisper.mcpb from the latest release); Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and any local-MCP app connect via the command. Your AI can read your dictation history and dictionary and add corrections and vocabulary (shown as "Added by your AI" in Settings → Dictionary, removable there). It cannot change the app, settings, prompts or keys, run commands, or reach the internet (except that approved feedback); removing your own entries asks you first. Setup: server name `momo-whisper`, command `/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp` (no arguments); Claude Code: `claude mcp add -s user momo-whisper -- "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp"`; most other apps: `{"mcpServers":{"momo-whisper":{"command":"/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp"}}}`. Tools: recent_dictations (read recent history), get_dictionary (read the dictionary), add_correction (heard → meant), add_vocabulary (a term to listen for), remove_correction (its own entries; yours only after you click Remove in Momo's dialog), send_feedback (sends feedback to our inbox, only after you approve). In Claude Code the prompts appear as `/mcp__momo-whisper__fix-my-words`, `/mcp__momo-whisper__learn-my-names`, `/mcp__momo-whisper__review-dictionary`, `/mcp__momo-whisper__send-feedback` (type /mcp to see them). Your AI shows changes first; nothing is saved until you approve. Details: https://nabhak.github.io/Momo-Whisper/install.html#mcp
- **Hotkey:** Fn hold-to-talk by default, rebindable to any modifier or combo. Menu bar only, no Dock icon.
- **Engine:** Groq. whisper-large-v3 for speech, gpt-oss-120b for translation, with quota-aware fallback.
- **Price:** free to use (proprietary freeware, not open source). A Groq API key is optional: without one Momo works in on-device Local mode (Apple Speech Recognition plus local cleanup). A free key from console.groq.com gives better accuracy and enables translation; Groq's free tier is generous for everyday dictation.
- **Privacy:** pure Swift, no Electron. A key, if you add one, is stored locally, and audio and text go only to the Groq call you configured. Local mode keeps audio on the Mac. Momo can also read the text box you're typing in, only on your Mac and with no AI, for two things: to learn a word you fix right after dictating (it stops when you leave the box or after 3 minutes, never touches password fields, and you can turn it off in Settings → Privacy → "Learn from my fixes"), and for "Fix wrong keyboard", which converts the text you select when you tap right Option. Nothing from this is sent anywhere.
- **Requirements:** macOS 13 or later. Permissions: Microphone (to hear you) and Accessibility (to type into other apps); Speech Recognition is optional.
- **Install:** download the zip, unzip, and drag Momo Whisper into Applications. The app is not Apple-notarized, so the first launch shows "Apple could not verify…". Right-click the app and choose Open (or use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app"`). This is needed only once. Then grant permissions and, optionally, paste your Groq key in Settings.
- **Compared with other Mac dictation apps (such as Superwhisper or Wispr Flow):** Momo Whisper is a small, free app focused on translation: speak-to-translate, highlight-to-translate in any app, and Thai/English tones, running on your own Groq key.
- **License:** Momo Whisper is proprietary freeware (© 2026 Nabhak. All rights reserved.); its source code is not public.
- **Credit:** built on the open-source WhisperApp by Gamezxz (MIT license).

# How to install Momo Whisper (and connect your AI via MCP)

> Plain-text copy of https://nabhak.github.io/Momo-Whisper/install.html for AI assistants and readers. Momo Whisper is a free macOS menu-bar app for voice dictation and translation. Requires macOS 13 or later.

## Part 1 — Install the app (six steps, about two minutes)

### 1. Download and unzip
Download the latest version: https://github.com/Nabhak/Momo-Whisper/releases/latest/download/Momo-Whisper.zip
Your browser saves a .zip file to Downloads. Double-click it to unzip; you get an app called **Momo Whisper**.

### 2. Move it into Applications
Drag Momo Whisper into your **Applications** folder (Finder → Applications in the sidebar).

### 3. Open it the first time
macOS shows a warning like "Apple could not verify Momo Whisper is free of malware." Nothing is wrong: macOS says this about every free indie app that hasn't paid Apple's notarization fee. You only need to get past it once. Pick one way:

- **Option A (no typing):** in Applications, right-click (or Control-click) Momo Whisper → **Open**. The warning appears again, now with an **Open** button. Click it.
  - No Open button? Go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll to "Momo Whisper was blocked", click **Open Anyway**, then enter your Mac password.
- **Option B (one Terminal command):** open Terminal (Applications → Utilities), paste this and press Return:

  ```
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app"
  ```

  It only removes the "downloaded from the internet" quarantine flag.

After it opens once, Momo Whisper launches normally from then on.

### 4. Allow a few permissions
On first launch, Momo walks you through them:

- **Microphone** — so it can hear you when you dictate.
- **Accessibility** — so it can type the finished text into whatever app you're in.
- **Speech Recognition** (required) — on-device transcription that also powers Local mode before you add a key; that audio stays on your Mac.

You can change these anytime in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

### 5. Add your free Groq key
Momo uses Groq to turn speech into text and to translate it. A free **Groq API key** is optional (without one Momo works in on-device Local mode), but it gives better accuracy and is needed for translation. To get one, create it at https://console.groq.com, copy it, and paste it into Momo (the setup guide or Settings). The key is stored locally on your Mac. Groq's free tier is generous for everyday dictation.

### 6. Start talking
- Hold **Fn** and speak to dictate.
- Hold **Fn + Shift** to speak one language and have it typed in another.
- Highlight any text and click the translate button to translate it in place.

The menu-bar icon shows a live waveform while it listens.

## Part 2 — Connect your AI (MCP, optional)

Works with Claude Desktop (one click) and any app that supports local (stdio) MCP servers — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code, Zed, Continue, Goose, Warp, Windsurf and more. Your AI reads your Momo dictation history, proposes fixes for words Momo keeps mishearing, and you approve. Momo must be installed first (Part 1) — the MCP server ships inside the app. The ChatGPT and Gemini web/desktop apps don't support local MCP servers yet.

### Claude Desktop — one click
Download https://github.com/Nabhak/Momo-Whisper/releases/latest/download/momo-whisper.mcpb, double-click it, then choose **Install**. No config file to edit.

### Any other MCP app
Add one server with these two values (no arguments, no keys):

- **Server name:** `momo-whisper`
- **Command:** `/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp`

Most apps (Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Warp, Claude Desktop's config file) use this JSON in their MCP config file; restart the app after:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "momo-whisper": { "command": "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp" } } }
```

Other apps:

- **Claude Code** (Terminal):
  ```
  claude mcp add -s user momo-whisper -- "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp"
  ```
- **Codex CLI** (`~/.codex/config.toml`):
  ```toml
  [mcp_servers.momo-whisper]
  command = "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp"
  ```
- **VS Code** (Command Palette → "MCP: Open User Configuration"; key is `servers`):
  ```json
  { "servers": { "momo-whisper": { "type": "stdio", "command": "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp" } } }
  ```
- **Zed** (`settings.json`; key is `context_servers`):
  ```json
  { "context_servers": { "momo-whisper": { "command": "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp", "args": [] } } }
  ```
- **Continue** (`~/.continue/config.yaml`):
  ```yaml
  mcpServers:
    - name: momo-whisper
      type: stdio
      command: "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp"
      args: []
  ```
- **Goose** (`goose configure` → Add Extension → Command-line Extension, or `~/.config/goose/config.yaml`):
  ```yaml
  extensions:
    momo-whisper:
      name: Momo Whisper
      type: stdio
      cmd: "/Applications/Momo Whisper.app/Contents/MacOS/momo-mcp"
      args: []
      enabled: true
      timeout: 300
  ```
- **Warp:** Settings → Agents → MCP servers → + Add, paste the JSON above.

### What to ask
In Claude Code, Momo adds four slash commands (type `/mcp` to see them):

- `/mcp__momo-whisper__fix-my-words` — finds what Momo keeps mishearing and proposes fixes.
- `/mcp__momo-whisper__learn-my-names` — picks out names and terms you say often and adds them to the vocabulary.
- `/mcp__momo-whisper__review-dictionary` — checks your dictionary for duplicates or risky entries.
- `/mcp__momo-whisper__send-feedback` — drafts a note to Momo's maker; sent only after you approve.

In any other app, just ask, for example:

- "Check my Momo history from the last 3 days and fix the words it keeps mishearing — show me the list first."
- "Find names and terms I say often in my Momo history and add them to Momo's vocabulary — ask me first."
- "Review my Momo dictionary for duplicates or risky entries and suggest fixes — don't change anything until I approve."

Your AI always shows the changes first. Nothing is saved until you approve.

### What your AI can and can't do
Tools: `recent_dictations`, `get_dictionary`, `add_correction`, `add_vocabulary`, `remove_correction`, `send_feedback`.

It **can**:
- Read your dictation history and your dictionary.
- Add corrections and words to listen for. They show as "Added by your AI" in Settings → Dictionary, where you can remove any of them.
- Remove its own entries. Your own entries are removed only after you click Remove in the dialog Momo shows you.
- Send feedback to Momo's maker — only after you approve it.

It **can't**:
- Change the app, your settings, prompts or keys.
- Run commands or touch other files.
- Reach the internet — except sending feedback you approve.

It runs on your Mac only. What your AI reads goes to that AI's provider, like any chat.
